messages:
maya: quick thread — noticed the judge ensemble tie rate jumped to ~28% on the quantized model bring-up run. rolling CI flagged it. can we triage?
aj: saw that in the dashboard, weirdly concentrated on open-domain QA slice. not uniform.
anika: link to dashboard?
maya: https://internal-redwood/dashboard/evals/2026/212345 — filter 'tie_rate' and 'quant=8bit'
liam: eval-runner posted a failing job too: 

eval-runner: job 2026-03-20-2123 FAILED — metric: tie_rate=0.281, agreement=0.63, logit_gap_mean=0.04

aj: low logit gap suggests judges are very uncertain. could be quantization noise making outputs more similar.
jamal: can we do a cheap tiebreaker using calibration score or entropy? i.e., if judges tie, pick candidate with lower avg entropy.
anika: entropy might be noisy across prompts. maybe prefer a trusted judge model (higher temp? higher capacity) as tiebreaker — but costy. we need an automated, lightweight proxy.
liam: idea: compute pairwise rank by mean logit gap across judges, then if tie use the candidate with higher mean rank. effectively a soft tiebreaker based on margin.
maya: we've tried logit_gap_mean but with quant it collapsed. need something robust to quant perturbation. maybe use nll on a non-quantized reference judge?
aj: running a non-quantified judge for every decision doubles cost. but could run only for ties (rare) as a fallback.
jamal: also want to keep bias checks — on demographic slices ties spike differently. check 'gender' slice in that run.
anika: ran quick slice check: ties on 'occupation' and 'safety' prompts increased more than others. not just gender.
liam: could be prompt-sensitive artifacts introduced during 8-bit kernels. let's reproduce locally with the eval harness and toggled quant flags.
maya: action plan: 1) liam reproduce with harness and dump logits/entropy across judges for tied examples 2) aj run slice-level tie diagnostics 3) jamal prototype cheap fallback: single-reference judge call only for ties 4) anika add CI gating threshold (tie_rate>0.2) to block rollout until we confirm mitigation
aj: i'll wire the CI gating as a soft alert first (doesn't block), we need to observe for a day before hard block.
liam: starting local run now. will post logs snippet.
liam: logs snippet: ```
# tied example id: 9832
judge_a logits: [2.1,2.09,2.08] entropy: 1.09
judge_b logits: [1.9,1.89,1.88] entropy: 1.12
judge_c logits: [2.0,2.0,1.99] entropy: 1.11
```
maya: margins tiny. looks like quant reduced precision just enough to flip ranks intermittently.
jamal: prototype fallback ready: call "ref-judge" only when tie occurs; default ref-judge is fp16 baseline. i'd like ux approval for cost bump.
anika: can we instead try smoothing logits with temperature scaling per judge before voting? less cost than ref call.
aj: temperature scaling seems promising — calibrates confidence. let's add a quick experiment: temperature in [0.8,1.0,1.2] and see tie_rate delta.
liam: running temp sweep now. also capturing slice-level diffs.
maya: also add a metric: tie_persistence — fraction of examples that remain tied across N>5 seeds. helps detect brittle ties vs genuine ambiguity.
jamal: good metric. add to dashboard and to CI report.
anika: one more: CI should log the fallback usage count and cost estimate so product knows the impact.
aj: agreed. i'll add those fields to the nightly eval summary.
liam: temp sweep results (prelim): temp=0.8 tie_rate=0.22, temp=1.0 tie_rate=0.28, temp=1.2 tie_rate=0.25. 0.8 helps but increases false positives on safety prompts slightly.
maya: we need a composite policy then: try temp-scaling at 0.8 + tie-fallback to ref-judge on safety/sensitive slices.
jamal: i'll implement fallback routing: if slice in {safety,legal,medical} and tie -> call ref-judge, else apply temp=0.8 smoothing and use margin tiebreaker.
anika: timeline?
jamal: PR for routing by EOD, tests tomorrow.
liam: will re-run full harness with routing rules and report tie_persistence and cost delta.
maya: perfect. thanks everyone. will follow up tomorrow with updated dashboard widgets. :thumbsup:
